title: What should a brand specify before producing a custom T-shirt?
seoTitle: Custom T-Shirt Production Checklist for Brands
description: Brief a T-shirt beyond its fabric and colour. Check the neckline, sleeve opening, seam behaviour and artwork position on the intended size range.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: A custom T-shirt looks simple until you compare two samples side by side. A few changes to neck width, sleeve angle or fabric drape can turn the same sketch into a different garment. Start your brief with the intended wearer and the one feature customers should notice when they put it on.

toc.text: Set the neckline before judging the whole tee
Use the first sample as a working sheet
Where should you position a chest print if the tee comes in several sizes?

bodyHtml:
Set the neckline before judging the whole tee

A close rib neck can make a wide body look more structured. A wider opening creates a different impression even if the chest measurement stays unchanged. Specify the neck shape, rib width as seen when finished and how you want the join to look. Check that the opening is comfortable to pull on and returns to the intended shape.

Use the first sample as a working sheet

AreaWhat to specifyCheck on the final garment
JerseyComposition, colour, weight and hand feelDrape, opacity in use and the surface available for the graphic
Shoulder and sleeveSeam position, sleeve length and openingWhere the sleeve ends with the arm resting naturally
Side and bottom seamsConstruction and finished hem depthWhether seams hang evenly before and after agreed care
Neck and labelsRib shape, label type and placementComfort against the skin and an easy-to-read size

Check artwork across sizes

Print the graphic on paper at intended scale and hold it against the smallest and largest sample available. This is a placement check, not a substitute for a decoration trial. When the position feels right, write the finished width, centre line and distance from a named seam. Ask the maker to confirm printable space if the artwork approaches a side seam or neck rib.

For a light tee with a large solid print, check how it hangs when worn. The decoration may affect the way the front moves, even if its colour looks right on the table. Test the proposed artwork on the fabric that will actually go into production.

Where should you position a chest print if the tee comes in several sizes?

Start with a named landmark such as the centre front or the neck seam. Place a paper version of the actual print on the smallest and largest available samples. If a single dimension makes one size look unbalanced, record which sizes use a different placement or artwork scale. Include those exceptions on the production sheet.

Prepare a short approval note

Write down which fabric, pattern and artwork versions were reviewed. If a care trial changes the length or causes the seam to twist, identify the garment and the measurement rather than approving from a fresh replacement photo. Keep one approved tee for the next reorder. For a sample review with BEWE4R, send your technical drawing, size range and the artwork at intended scale.
